headline: Ramco Cements files Scheme of Amalgamation with NSE
sum: Ramco Cements, a listed cement manufacturer, notified the NSE on 20 June 2026 of a Scheme of Amalgamation under the Companies Act 2013, signalling a merger or consolidation; NCLT approval and shareholder sanction are pending, with scheme details and consideration valuation yet to be disclosed publicly.
implication: A listed cement consolidation of this nature will require dual-track approval-NCLT sanction (Sections 230–232) and shareholder resolution (Section 110)-and may trigger stock exchange listing rules for material related-party transactions and disclosure timelines; monitor NCLT Regional Bench filings and follow-up scheme amendments for consideration structure and merger accounting treatment.
detail: Ramco Cements Limited, a major Indian cement manufacturer with multi-state operations, disclosed a Scheme of Amalgamation to NSE on 20 June 2026 indicating structural reorganisation. The scheme document, filed with the exchange as per Listing Rules disclosure norms, sets out merging entities, consideration, and effective date; however, the target entity name and deal valuation have not been disclosed in the announcement stub. Standard regulatory pathway requires NCLT approval under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act 2013 and shareholder sanction under Section 110; timeline and identities of the amalgamating company and the transferee company remain pending corroboration from NCLT filings or company press release.

framework.note: NCLT approval required for scheme of amalgamation; merging entity must petition Regional Bench with scheme, balance sheet, and statutory declarations.
Shareholder approval in general meeting required for scheme; voting threshold and order of NCLT petition / approval sequence must be adhered to.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 2015, Regulation 30 & Schedule III
framework.note: Listed company must disclose scheme of amalgamation as material event within 30 minutes of board decision; scheme details including consideration must be disclosed in timely manner post-filing.
Merger under scheme of amalgamation qualifies for tax-neutral transfer of assets if conditions met; stamp duty implications on transfer of assets.
Fair valuation and accounting treatment of amalgamation assets and liabilities; independent valuer may be required.

framework.ref: National Company Law Tribunal Rules 2016, Part C (Scheme Petitions)
framework.note: Procedural rules for filing and hearing of scheme petition; advertisement and creditor claims timeline.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations 2011, Regulation 3(a)–3(g)
framework.note: If amalgamation results in change of control post-merger, takeover code disclosure and open offer obligations may be triggered.
Duty on conveyance of property under scheme; state-level stamp duty variations apply to transfer of real estate / assets.

conditions: NCLT approval under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act 2013

Creditor approval and claims process (if triggered under NCLT Rules 2016)

approvals: NCLT Regional Bench sanction (on petition to be filed)

triggers.note: Scheme of amalgamation requires NCLT sanction; petition filing and order approval are gating items.
Material event disclosure to exchange; scheme announcement, updates, and approval milestones must be disclosed timely.
Tax-neutral treatment available if conditions met; proper documentation and compliance required.
If post-merger shareholding results in change of control, open offer may be mandated.
